steps.title: Let's start with the basics
steps.subtitle: Three quick questions, then we'll take a look at the room.

targets.instruction: What are you hoping to do?
targets.rationale: Sets the overall shape of the job and determines which later targets apply.

options.label: Freshen it up — tiles, paint, small changes

targets.instruction: When would you like the work to start?
targets.rationale: Timing disqualifies a job faster than almost anything else. Contractors need it in the triage header.

options.label: Within the next month or two

targets.instruction: Who should buy the bath, tiles and taps?
targets.hint: Most people ask the contractor to handle it.
targets.rationale: Material supply responsibility changes the quote fundamentally and is the most common cause of quotes that cannot be compared.

options.label: The contractor — I'd rather they sorted it

steps.title: Let's take a look at your bathroom
steps.subtitle: Stand in the doorway to start. We'll tell you where to point.

targets.subject: space.bathroom
targets.instruction: Start at the doorway and slowly turn all the way around
targets.hint: Nice and slow — about ten seconds for a full turn.
targets.rationale: One continuous pass gives contractors context and adjacency that a set of stills never conveys. Also the primary frame source for future detection work.

targets.subject: space.bathroom.wall_left
targets.instruction: Now show us the wall on your left
targets.rationale: Wall-by-wall stills give tiling extent, condition and fixture positions at usable resolution.

targets.subject: space.bathroom.wall_ahead
targets.instruction: Now the wall straight ahead of you
targets.rationale: As above.

targets.subject: space.bathroom.wall_right
targets.instruction: And the wall on your right
targets.rationale: As above.

targets.subject: space.bathroom.ceiling
targets.instruction: Point the camera up and show us the ceiling
targets.rationale: Ceiling condition, staining from leaks above, extractor and lighting positions.

targets.subject: space.bathroom.floor
targets.instruction: Now point it down at the floor
targets.rationale: Existing floor finish, levels, and whether the substrate is timber or solid.

steps.title: Now the things in the room

targets.subject: element.bath
targets.instruction: Show us the bath or shower
targets.hint: Stand back far enough to get the whole thing and the wall behind it.
targets.rationale: Removal cost, tiling behind, existing taps and screen, waste position.

targets.subject: element.wc
targets.instruction: Show us the toilet
targets.rationale: Soil pipe position is the single biggest constraint on bathroom layout changes.

targets.subject: element.basin
targets.instruction: Show us the sink
targets.rationale: Type, mounting and existing supply positions.

targets.subject: element.basin.services
targets.instruction: Now crouch down and show us underneath the sink
targets.hint: We're looking at the pipes. Use the torch if it's dark.
targets.rationale: Existing pipework, isolation valves and waste arrangement. Requested by contractors on a large share of bathroom jobs, so it is a required target rather than something they have to ask for.

targets.subject: element.radiator
targets.instruction: Is there a radiator or towel rail? Show us that too
targets.rationale: Heating circuit position and pipe centres.

targets.subject: element.window
targets.instruction: Show us the window
targets.rationale: Reveal depth, sill, tiling around the opening, and ventilation.

targets.subject: element.door
targets.instruction: Show us the door, opened
targets.rationale: Access width for getting a bath in and rubble out, and door swing constraints on layout.

targets.instruction: If you have a boiler or a hot water tank nearby, show us that
targets.hint: A photo of the label on the front is really helpful.
targets.rationale: Determines achievable shower type and whether a pump is needed. Homeowners cannot answer this reliably, but they can photograph it.

targets.instruction: Is anything damaged, cracked or stained? Show us
targets.hint: Get close enough that we can see it clearly.
targets.rationale: Condition is the most common source of quote variance. Anything visible and unresolved becomes an open item.

steps.title: Let's get some measurements
steps.subtitle: This is the part contractors need most.

targets.subject: space.bathroom
targets.instruction: Walk slowly around the room with your camera up
targets.hint: We'll work out the size as you go.
targets.rationale: Tier A devices produce confirmed dimensions and an element inventory in one pass. Falls back silently to manual entry where unavailable.

targets.instruction: Measure this wall from corner to corner, along the floor
targets.rationale: Room length. A careful tape measurement is more accurate than a phone estimate, so this fallback is not a downgrade in quality.

targets.instruction: Now measure the other wall the same way
targets.rationale: Room width.

targets.instruction: Now measure from the floor to the ceiling
targets.rationale: Required for wall area and full-height tiling quantities.

targets.instruction: Does that look about right?
targets.rationale: Nothing produced by a sensor or a model reaches a contractor unconfirmed. 'No idea' is recorded honestly rather than forcing a false confirmation.

targets.subject: element.bath
targets.instruction: Are you keeping the bath?
targets.rationale: Core disposition. Drives strip-out, waste alterations and shower tray or enclosure work.

options.label: New bath in the same place
Taking it out and putting in a shower

targets.instruction: Would the shower go where the bath is now, or somewhere else?
targets.rationale: Relocation implies alterations to hot, cold and waste services, which is where bathroom budgets are won and lost. Always asked explicitly, never inferred.

targets.instruction: Are you moving the sink or toilet to a different position?
targets.rationale: Translates to first-fix plumbing alterations. Never ask the homeowner about first fix directly.

options.label: No, everything stays where it is

targets.instruction: Would you like tiles all the way up to the ceiling?
targets.rationale: Determines tile quantity and labour. Shown as a picture because the difference is obvious visually and hard to describe.

options.label: Just around the bath and sink
Not sure — what would you suggest?

targets.instruction: Are the walls cracked, damaged or uneven anywhere?
targets.rationale: Translates to substrate preparation. Never ask about substrate.

options.label: A few small cracks or bumps

targets.instruction: Which floor is the bathroom on?
targets.rationale: Access is where quotes go wrong. Floor, lift and parking change the job materially.

targets.instruction: Is there a lift?
targets.rationale: Manual handling of baths, tiles and waste up several flights is a significant cost.

targets.instruction: Where would a van park?
targets.rationale: Permit zones and restricted hours affect both price and scheduling.

options.label: On the street, but it's a permit area

targets.instruction: Will anyone be living there while the work happens?
targets.rationale: Occupied works mean dust protection, staged working and often a second bathroom question.

targets.instruction: Anything else you'd like contractors to know?
targets.hint: Tap the microphone and just talk — it's easier than typing.
targets.rationale: Homeowners disclose things here that no structured question would elicit, and contractors read it first. Attached to the pack verbatim, never rewritten.
